issues.issue: Was the judicial review application moot because the scheduled removal date passed while a stay was in place?
issues.applicant_position: Controversy stays live: deferral was sought pending the H&C decision, which is still outstanding.
issues.respondent_position: Also says not moot: the dispute is whether removal should occur before the pending H&C decision.
issues.result_quote: I have come to the conclusion that a live controversy still exists between the parties and that, as a result, the appellants’ judicial review application is not moot.

issues.issue: Should the Court exercise its discretion to hear the merits of the application even if it were moot?
issues.applicant_position: Alternatively, the Federal Court erred in declining to exercise its discretion to decide the merits.
issues.respondent_position: A merits decision would give a real remedy; a mootness finding lets stay motions prejudge the merits.
issues.result_quote: I would have had no hesitation in deciding that this Court ought to deal with the merits of the application

issues.issue: Was the enforcement officer’s refusal to defer removal pending the outstanding H&C application reasonable?
issues.applicant_position: Officer erred in refusing deferral pending the H&C decision; children’s best interests require deferral.
issues.respondent_position: Officer considered all circumstances, including the children; s.48 requires removal as soon as reasonably practicable.
issues.result_quote: I therefore conclude that the enforcement officer’s decision to refuse deferral of the appellants’ removal from Canada was reasonable and that the decision must stand.
